name: Natural bodybuilding (drug-tested)

lead: Natural bodybuilding is bodybuilding judged in federations that screen competitors for banned drugs, using polygraph interviews, urine tests and sometimes blood or hair tests. Competitors build muscle, symmetry and leanness through resistance training, nutrition and recovery.

For looksmaxxers it serves as a reference for what a drug-free physique can look like and how long it takes. It also supplies a contest-prep playbook of lean, defined, conditioned physiques; research on natural bodybuilders documents the dieting phases that produce that look.

paras: Competitors alternate off-season muscle-building with a gradual contest-prep fat-loss phase and a recovery phase. A sports-nutrition review recommends losing about 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight per week to retain muscle, with high protein intake. Federations vary in testing and drug-free requirements.
Contest preparation can be hard on the body and psychology; the review warns that final-days dehydration and electrolyte manipulation can be dangerous. Testing standards differ between federations.

chain: Train, eat and recover under a drug-free competition standard
Build muscle and reach contest-level leanness
angle.text: Natural bodybuilders show and use the methods of progressive training and structured dieting to maximise muscle and definition. Enthusiasts use their stats and prep practices to set realistic physique goals.

lead: Natural bodybuilding is competitive bodybuilding held under drug-testing rules, in contrast to untested federations where performance-enhancing drugs are common. Contestants are judged on muscularity, symmetry, conditioning and posing, as in other bodybuilding.[1][2]

For people interested in appearance it is both a goal and a benchmark: it demonstrates the lean, muscular physique reachable through training and diet without banned drugs, and its contest-prep methods are widely borrowed for cutting.[1][3]
Testing combines polygraph interviews about drug and supplement history with urinalysis, and some federations add blood or hair tests; penalties run from suspensions to lifetime bans.[1][2]

paras: Grokipedia credits Chet Yorton as the 'father of natural bodybuilding', who organised the first drug-tested US event, the American Natural Physique Championships, in 1978. The WNBF was founded in 1989 and held its first professional drug-tested contest in 1990; the PNBA followed in 1990 and the INBA in 1994, and together they run the Natural Olympia, first held in 1998.[1] Wikipedia notes that mainstream bodybuilding drew on organisations such as the IFBB and NPC, where the NPC does not require testing.[2]

Natural federations include WNBF, INBA/PNBA, NANBF, ANBF and OCB, most following WADA-style rules. Drug-free requirements vary, for example 10 years from prescription hormones in the WNBF and 7 years in the ANBF.[1]

A review of evidence-based natural contest preparation recommends losing about 0.5 to 1 percent of body weight per week, protein of 2.3 to 3.1 g per kg of lean mass, 15 to 30 percent of calories from fat, and notes creatine, caffeine and beta-alanine appear beneficial, while dehydration and electrolyte manipulation can be dangerous.[4] Case studies have followed natural bodybuilders through prep and recovery.[3]

Grokipedia describes violations at natural events, such as multiple failures at the 2010 Natural Universe, and debate over differing standards between federations.[1] Wikipedia notes social-media influencers often leave unclear whether they are natural, and that studies from the 2010s found higher mortality among bodybuilders.[2]

A 2014 review in the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition set out recommendations for natural contest preparation.[4] A 12-month case study examined natural bodybuilding preparation and recovery.[3] A case series tracked drug-free bodybuilders through off-season, pre-competition and recovery phases.
